n: Kadampanad St. Thomas Orthodox Cathedral & Historic Thomasine Pilgrim Centre
ds:
Established by migrants from Nilackal in 325 CE in the name of St. Thomas. Rebuilt in 800, 1200, 1800, 1912, 1952 CE. The church additionally grew in members from Nilackal refugees in the 12th and 14th centuries. This church has hundreds of daughter parishes, notably those at: Mavelikkara, Kayamkulam, Kollakadavu, Adoor, Kozhencherry, Kaipattoor, Sooranad, Kallada and Koodal. St. Gregorios of Parumala had a grand apostolic visit to this church in 1895.

Mar Thoma III of Kadampanad is entombed in the altar of this church.

The parish was declared a Marthoman Pilgrim Centre on 7 March 2010 by the Catholicos.

25 families (2022) – Situated in the rural village of Parasuvaikkal, approximately 300 meters from the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border, this church serves one of the southernmost Orthodox congregations in the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

Despite its small size, the parish maintains a vibrant Orthodox presence in this remote region. At least one priest of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church has come from this parish, reflecting its contribution to the life of the Church beyond its modest congregation.
Cemetery Chapel of the Nearby Parish.

400 families (2022) – With a history spanning more than 160 years, this is one of the oldest and most historically significant parishes of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese. Before a church existed in the region, the ascetic priest Younan Kaseesha, affectionately remembered as Anchal Achan, ministered to the Orthodox faithful while serving from Kottarakkara. As Christian families migrated to Anchal for agriculture, trade, and employment, the growing community established a simple thatched chapel dedicated to St. George on the Kandathil property, creating the first permanent Orthodox place of worship in the area.

Recognizing the need for a permanent church, community leaders petitioned the Malankara Metropolitan for permission to build a parish. In 1903, a church was erected on nearly one acre of land generously donated by the prominent advocate Elanjikkal Cherian Chacko (Varinjam Sir), together with the efforts of Changampallil Koruthu Vadyar and Mathai Mathunni. Rev. Fr. Abraham of Kundara Thenguvila became the first vicar, and the parish soon developed into the principal Orthodox church of the Anchal region.

The present church was consecrated in 1985 by H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros, the founding Metropolitan of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese, assisted by H.G. Geevarghese Mar Osthathios. Continued growth led to the construction of a meditation room dedicated to Anchal Achan (1990), a meditation hall and church porch (1998), a new clergy residence (2002), the Anchal Achan Memorial Parish Hall (2007), and a granite cross with landscaped entrance consecrated by H.G. Dr. Gabriel Mar Gregorios in 2013.

The parish maintains three prominent roadside shrines dedicated to St. George. The first was established along the Ayur–Anchal Road in 1965 on land donated by the late Mr. Krishnan Muthalali. A second shrine was constructed on the Anchal–Punalur Road in 1996 on land donated by the late Mr. E. John of the Elavukattu family. The third shrine was erected in 2005 along the Kadakkal–Chengamanad Road by the Punalur Changampallil family on land donated by the children of the late Mr. C. T. Samuel. A ceremonial flagmast sponsored by the Punalur Changampallil family was added to the church campus in 2009.

Recognizing its historical and spiritual importance, H.G. Dr. Gabriel Mar Gregorios proclaimed the parish as St. George Orthodox Valiyapally in 2009. On June 13, 2010, H.H. Baselios Marthoma Didymos I declared it a Georgian Pilgrimage Centre, acknowledging its importance as one of southern Kerala's principal centers of devotion to St. George.

Today, the parish serves more than 1,600 faithful across five panchayats—Anchal, Edamulakkal, Alayamon, Karavaloor, and Ittiva—and functions as the Mother Church of the region. Organized into eleven wards with seven active prayer groups, it sustains vibrant Sunday School, youth, women's, and spiritual organizations while maintaining extensive charitable ministries that provide assistance for housing, education, marriages, and medical needs regardless of caste or religion. The annual feasts of St. George and the revered Anchal Achan continue to attract large numbers of pilgrims from across southern Kerala.

13 families (2022) – Located on Market Road in Attingal, this parish serves the local Orthodox community despite its small congregation.

The church features three altars and a roadside shrine dedicated to St. George at its entrance, making it a visible landmark for the faithful in the town.

Holy Qurbana: Sunday, 8:30 AM

475 families (2022) – Established around 1755, this is one of the oldest Orthodox churches in southern Kerala and the oldest church in Chathannoor. Historically known as "Chathannoor Marthamariyam Suriyani Pally," it became the Mother Church of the Chathannoor region, from which numerous Orthodox parishes were later established. Today, it remains one of the largest parishes in the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

The church preserves an exceptional collection of historical artifacts spanning more than two centuries. Among its most treasured works is a rare 1792 mural of St. George, depicting the saint from an uncommon perspective unlike the traditional dragon-slaying iconography. The church also houses the historic Chathannoor Panchangam, written in both Malayalam and Tamil, which preserves important records of the Malankara Church and references to Mar Nicholas's visit to Kerala.

Another remarkable artifact is an 1861 painting by British Army Lieutenant Colonel Stevenson portraying Geevarghese Yacob Kattanar celebrating the Holy Qurbana while offering his sword, providing a rare visual record of nineteenth-century Malankara liturgical life. The church has also carefully preserved ancient stone lamps, candlestands, and other liturgical objects despite successive renovations. A massive stone oil lamp carved from a single block of granite still stands before the entrance and continues to attract devotees from different faiths who light lamps there in prayer.

More than two and a half centuries after its founding, the church remains one of the foremost centers of Orthodox worship and heritage in southern Kerala, preserving the liturgical, artistic, and historical traditions of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

n: Cheruvakkal St. Gregorios Orthodox Qurbana Centre
ds: A church under Cheruvakkal St. George Parish.

45 families (2022) – Located in Chittazha on the northeastern edge of the Thiruvananthapuram metropolitan area, this parish serves the growing Orthodox community of the surrounding suburbs.

Although the parish is relatively new, many Orthodox families in the area continue to retain their membership at the historic Palayam Cathedral, resulting in a smaller local congregation. The church's modern design and strategic location position it for continued growth as the northeastern suburbs of the city continue to expand.

n: Kazhakuttom St. Mary's and St. Jude Orthodox Church
ds:
60 families (2022) – This parish serves the Orthodox community of Kazhakuttom, a major IT and residential hub in Thiruvananthapuram.

Although established to cater to the growing local population, a significant portion of Orthodox families in the area continue to remain under the jurisdiction of St. George Orthodox Cathedral, Palayam. As a result, the parish is still in a phase of gradual consolidation and outreach, working to strengthen its base among residents who have recently settled in the region due to the expansion of the IT sector and associated urban development.

n: Kodunganoor St. Gregorios Orthodox Mission Centre
ds:
Established under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in the name of St. Gregorios of Parumala, this rehabilitation center provides comprehensive support for economically disadvantaged persons with disabilities through institution-based care and community outreach.

The center conducts surveys to identify individuals in need, provides counseling, facilitates medical treatment, corrective surgeries, physiotherapy, prosthetic devices, and other rehabilitation services, and promotes disability prevention through public awareness programs.

It also supports economic independence by offering financial assistance, small-business loans, and vocational training, including tailoring, electronics repair, and other practical skills, enabling persons with disabilities to achieve greater self-sufficiency.

92 families (2022) – Located in Kowdiar, the most affluent residential area of Thiruvananthapuram, this church serves the Orthodox community of one of the city's most prominent neighborhoods.

The church houses an IAS academy in its basement, providing educational support and civil service preparation alongside its parish ministry.

The parish received widespread attention following an Onam celebration held inside the church that featured a performer portraying Mahabali, sparking significant public controversy and discussion within sections of the Orthodox community.

n: Kulasekharam St. Thomas Malankara Orthodox Church
ds:
66 families (2022) – This church serves the Malankara Orthodox Malayali community in the Kanyakumari region, providing a spiritual home for families who migrated from Kerala.

The parish operates a student hostel and includes a roadside shrine dedicated to the Virgin Mary at the entrance to the church.

431 families (2022) – Established as a filial parish of the Palayam Cathedral, this church serves one of the larger Orthodox congregations in Thiruvananthapuram.

Despite its size, the church accommodates only about 350 worshippers at a time—roughly 17% of its approximately 2,100 members—with additional capacity available during major feast days. Attendance is highest during weddings, baptisms, funerals, Christmas, Good Friday, and Easter.

For many years, the parish was shepherded by Very Rev. Fr. Alexander Vaidyan Cor-Episcopa, who served as its longest-tenured vicar.

Situated on one of the highest elevations around Thiruvananthapuram, this cemetery and chapel serve the burial needs of Thekkan Parumala St. Peter's & St. Paul's Orthodox Church.

Its hilltop setting provides sweeping views of the surrounding landscape, making it one of the region's most scenic Orthodox cemeteries. Access is by a steep uphill road, which can become difficult for low-clearance vehicles, particularly during the monsoon season.

The cemetery chapel continues to host funeral services, memorial prayers, and other liturgical observances for the parish community.

Established as the cemetery chapel of St. Thomas Orthodox Church, Kumarapuram, this chapel serves the parish burial grounds at Malamukal.

Located on the outskirts of Thiruvananthapuram, the cemetery was developed after affordable land became available on the surrounding hilltops, providing space for future burials beyond the increasingly land-constrained city.

The chapel continues to serve funeral services, memorial prayers, and other liturgical observances associated with the parish cemetery.

n: Malayinkeezh St. Gregorios Orthodox Mission Church
ds:
22 families (2022) – This mission church serves the Orthodox community of Malayinkeezh while supporting the missionary outreach of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

Beyond its liturgical ministry, the parish is dedicated to serving underprivileged families through charitable initiatives, providing care, assistance, and compassionate support to those in need within the local community.

n: Nagercoil St. George Malankara Orthodox Church
ds: 10 families (2022) – Located in Suriyani Nasrani Nagar, this church serves the Malayali Orthodox families who have settled in Nagercoil, particularly those residing in the area's historic Malayali Syrian Christian neighborhood.

This cemetery chapel serves the burial grounds of St. Mary's Orthodox Church, Nalanchira, and hosts funeral services, memorial prayers, and other liturgical observances for the parish.

Located beside one of the largest Malankara Catholic cemeteries in the region, the cemetery had 77 faithful interred here as of 2017 and continues to serve the growing needs of the parish community.

378 families (2025), 521 families (2022) – Originally established as a filial chapel of the Palayam Cathedral, this church has developed into one of the major Orthodox parishes in the eastern part of Thiruvananthapuram.

The parish traces its beginnings to a chapel established to serve the Orthodox students and staff of the nearby Mar Ivanios College. Today, it continues to uphold this legacy of faith and learning while expanding into a vibrant parish community.

Serving approximately 1,812 faithful across six parish wards, the church remains an important center of worship, pastoral care, and community life for Orthodox families in the rapidly growing Nalanchira region. The parish is presently served by two priests, ensuring regular liturgical services and pastoral ministry for the faithful.

74 families (2022) – Established as a daughter parish of the Palayam Cathedral, this church serves the Orthodox community with a close-knit congregation.

The church enshrines the Holy Relics of Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni), making it a place of particular spiritual significance.

Before the present church was constructed, the site functioned as an active diocesan youth development center. Today, the parish celebrates the Holy Qurbana every Sunday from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m., followed by breakfast for the faithful.

n: Palavilai St. George Tamil Orthodox Church
ds:
85 families (2022) – This mission church serves the Tamil Orthodox community of Palavilai and is one of the principal centers of the Malankara Orthodox mission among the ethnic Tamil population of Kanyakumari.

All liturgical services, prayers, and parish activities are conducted in Tamil, reflecting the linguistic and cultural heritage of the congregation.

105 students (2025) – Established in 1975 under the leadership of L.L. H.G. Philipose Mar Theophilos, this MGOCSM center became a pioneering model for Orthodox student ministry in Kerala.

Its first warden, Rev. Dn. George Kurien, later H.G. Geevarghese Mar Coorilos, transformed a repurposed residence into a dedicated center for student life and spiritual formation.

Today, the center continues to serve Orthodox students through residential accommodation, theological formation, and community life, remaining one of the flagship institutions of the MGOCSM.

Consecrated in 1977 by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews I, this chapel forms the spiritual heart of the MGOCSM center in Thiruvananthapuram.

The consecration of the expanded complex, including the chapel, auditorium, and guest facilities, was attended by international ecumenical representatives, reflecting its significance within Orthodox student ministry.

The chapel continues to host regular worship and serves as a center for the liturgical and spiritual life of Orthodox students.

Established in 1975 during a period of ecclesiastical realignment, this church emerged as a distinct Patriarchal congregation in Thiruvananthapuram. Its present church was consecrated on February 13–14, 1982, by Patriarch Ignatius Zakka I Iwas and has since been administered under the 1979 Patriarchal constitution.

The parish serves more than 250 families and oversees several charitable institutions, including a special-needs school, two cemeteries, and a cross shrine at Pongumoodu, which was elevated to parish status in 2003.

Its first leader was a lay acolyte ordained to the priesthood within four months without formal seminary formation, a decision widely criticized as a significant departure from established ecclesiastical discipline.

n: Parottukonam St. Thomas Karunya Monastery & Convent
ds:
This monastery and convent serves as a center of prayer, monastic life, and charitable ministry under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. A Ramban resides here alongside monks and nuns who oversee the institution's spiritual and social outreach.

The complex houses the St. Thomas Karunya Guidance Centre and serves as the administrative center for Karunya Vishranti Bhavan, a palliative care center, an old-age home, the Karunya Snehabhojanam food assistance program, the Karunya Sick Aid Foundation, and a marriage assistance foundation. Together, these ministries provide healthcare, financial assistance, and compassionate support to vulnerable members of society.

This chapel forms part of the St. Thomas Karunya Guidance Centre, serving as the spiritual heart of the monastery's charitable ministries and providing regular liturgical services for its residents, staff, and the surrounding Orthodox community.

The foundation stone was laid on August 24, 1986, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews I, Catholicos of the East and Malankara Metropolitan, marking the beginning of the center's spiritual and charitable mission.

Located on prime land in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, this cemetery is the historic burial ground of the Palayam Cathedral and contains more than 5,000 interments.

Having reached full capacity, most new burials are now conducted at Malamukal. Families with relatives already interred here, however, may continue to use existing family burial plots.

A weekly service is held every Saturday at the Pattoor Cemetery Chapel, with Morning Prayer at 6:30 a.m. followed by the Holy Qurbana at 7:00 a.m.

60 families (2022) – This church is the first in Kerala and the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church to be dedicated to Saint Dionysius, giving it a unique place in the church's history.

Sunday Holy Mass is celebrated starting at 06:30 AM.

Though presently a small parish, it continues to grow and has long been envisioned as a future pilgrimage center dedicated to the legacy of the saint. Expansion of the church and its facilities remains a long-term objective.

Established under the Palayam Cathedral, this shrine was built to serve the Orthodox faithful of the Plammoodu area.

It was founded as a votive offering by a parishioner who credited St. George with saving his life after a snakebite. The shrine also enshrines icons of the Virgin Mary and Jesus Christ, making it a place of prayer and devotion for the local community.

n: Pooyappally St. Peter's and St. Paul's Orthodox Church

ds:
Located in the rural outskirts north of Thiruvananthapuram, this monastery serves as a center of Orthodox monastic life, prayer, and spiritual formation. The peaceful setting provides an environment well suited for silent prayer and contemplation while preserving the ascetic traditions of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church in Kerala's capital region.

The monastery is home to several religious brothers (celibate priests). It also serves as the present residence of H.G. Gabriel Mar Gregorios, Metropolitan of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese, making it an important spiritual center of the diocese.

n: Sreekariyam Holy Cross Convent & St. George Orthodox Chapel (Alathara)
ds:
This convent serves as a center of prayer, monastic life, and Christian service under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. The resident sisters oversee the adjoining St. George Orthodox Chapel while carrying out ministries of education, worship, and community outreach.

The convent also administers Holy Trinity English Medium Higher Secondary School, one of the major educational institutions of the Thiruvananthapuram Orthodox Diocese, continuing the Church's longstanding commitment to academic excellence and Christian values.

is chapel serves as the spiritual center of the St. Thomas Karunya Monastery and Karunya Vishranti Bhavan, providing daily worship for the monastery's resident clergy, religious, and approximately 50 inmates of the care home.

Regular evening prayers are conducted every day, while Holy Qurbana is celebrated on Sundays.

n: Sreekariyam St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory Orthodox Church
ds:
251 families (2022) – Established as an independent parish in 1985, this church traces its origins to a congregation formed in 1978 by families of the Palayam St. George Orthodox Cathedral who had settled in the Sreekariyam area.

Before the parish was established, the faithful gathered for prayer in their homes while a temporary building at the present site served as both a Sunday School and place of worship. H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros formally established the parish on July 17, 1985, dedicating it to the Cappadocian Fathers, St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory.

The present church was constructed and consecrated on February 3–4, 2000, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II, Catholicos of the East and Malankara Metropolitan. Today, it continues to serve as one of the principal Orthodox parishes in northern Thiruvananthapuram.

This monastery serves as a center of Orthodox monastic life and charitable ministry under the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church. Home to a resident monk and nun, it oversees Karunya Vishranti Bhavan, a major humanitarian institution established in 1998 to provide compassionate care for the poor, the sick, and the abandoned.

The campus offers hospice and palliative care for terminally ill cancer patients, residential care for elderly and homeless individuals, psychosocial rehabilitation for people with mental illness, support for those living with HIV/AIDS, a primary healthcare clinic, and a day-care program for the local poor. Patients and residents are provided accommodation, meals, medical assistance, counseling, and spiritual care regardless of caste, religion, or social background.

n: Thiruvithamcode St. Mary's Malankara Orthodox Church
ds:
12 families (2022) - Traditionally believed to have been consecrated by Saint Thomas the Apostle in AD 63, this church is revered as one of the Ezharappallikal (Seven and a Half Churches) established during his missionary journey after arriving in India around AD 52. It remains one of the oldest and most significant centers of St. Thomas Christian heritage.

Known as Arappally or Thomayar Kovil, the church is traditionally called the "Half Church" because Saint Thomas is believed to have initially established only a cross or simple place of prayer for the first Christian families. Another tradition associates the name with a "Royal Church," reflecting the patronage of the King of Venad, who granted land for its construction.

Unlike most ancient churches of India, this church preserves much of its original architectural character. Constructed from locally quarried granite blocks, it incorporates features common to early South Indian temple architecture, including granite pillars, wooden foyers, terracotta roofing, and a sanctuary resembling the traditional Sreekovil. Among its surviving antiquities are an ancient baptismal font, a Portuguese hanging lamp, a historic censer, a two-thousand-year-old well that has never run dry, and a stone cross traditionally attributed to Saint Thomas.

For nearly two millennia, this church has remained a continuous place of Christian worship and is traditionally regarded as one of the oldest church structures in the world still holding daily prayers. It is maintained by the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church and was proclaimed an International St. Thomas Pilgrimage Centre on December 16, 2007, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Didymos I.

According to local tradition, the early Christian community endured severe persecution after its establishment. A woman remembered as Chirutha is said to have organized a force known as the Chirutha Pada to defend the newly converted Christians, becoming a lasting figure in the region's Christian heritage.

Today, the church remains one of the foremost pilgrimage destinations of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, drawing thousands of pilgrims, historians, and visitors each year to one of the most historically significant Christian sites in India.

50 families (2022) – Located along one of the principal roads in the heart of Thiruvananthapuram, this independent chapel serves a thriving Orthodox congregation despite its canonical status as a chapel. Commonly known as Holy Trinity Church, Ulloor, it functions much like a parish church, providing regular liturgical services and pastoral care.

The chapel is also home to Holy Trinity Media, an Orthodox media ministry that supports the Church's evangelistic and educational outreach through digital and multimedia initiatives.

Since 1986, this Orthodox Center has served as the official episcopal residence of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

Established through the vision of H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros, the center occupies a central location in Ulloor while providing a peaceful setting for prayer, administration, and diocesan ministry. It continues to function as an important administrative and spiritual hub of the diocese.

n: Vadakkankulam St. Thomas Malankara Orthodox Church
ds:
7 families (2022) – Established to serve the Orthodox students of the S. A. Raja College campus in Vadakkankulam, Tirunelveli district, this church ministers to nearly 500 students pursuing professional and higher education in fields including medicine, dentistry, engineering, nursing, pharmacy, management, and education.

The land for the church was donated by Sardar Dr. S. A. Raja, founder and chairman of the Rajas Colleges, on August 27, 2008. The foundation stone was laid by H.G. Dr. Gabriel Mar Gregorios, Metropolitan of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese, and the church was consecrated on October 29–30, 2010.

n: Vattiyoorkavu St. Peter's & St. Paul's Orthodox Church
ds:
189 families (2022) - 189 families (2022) – This church was established as the 101st parish (before the diocesan bifurcation) of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese and became the sixth Malankara Orthodox parish founded within Thiruvananthapuram city.

Since its establishment, it has served the growing Orthodox community of the Vattiyoorkavu region and remains an integral part of the expanding ecclesiastical presence of the diocese in the easternmost inland areas of the state capital.

n: Velimala St. George Malankara Orthodox Church
ds:

Despite its tiny congregation, the parish maintains a continuous Orthodox presence, providing regular worship and pastoral care for the local faithful.

ഫാദർ ആൻഡ്രോണികിന്റെ സ്വസ്ഥമായുള്ള സന്യാസ ജീവിതത്തിനുള്ള ആഗ്രഹ പ്രകാരം തോമാ മാർ ദീവന്നാസ്യോസ് അദ്ദേഹത്തെ പത്തനാപുരത്തിനടുത്തുള്ള പട്ടാഴി ഗ്രാമത്തിൽ 'മധുരമല' എന്ന ഒരു ഉയർന്ന പ്രദേശത്ത് പള്ളിയും ആശ്രമവും സ്ഥാപിക്കുന്നതിൽ സഹായിച്ചു. മധുരമലയിൽ പള്ളി സ്ഥാപിക്കുന്നതിൽ ഫാദർ ആൻഡ്രോണികിനെ സഹായിക്കുവാൻ തോമാ മാർ ദീവന്നാസ്യോസ് തിരുമേനി യോഹന്നാൻ കശ്ശീശായെയാണ് നിയോഗിച്ചത്. ആദ്യനാളുകളിൽ ഫാദർ ആൻഡ്രോണിക്ക് ഒരു മരക്കുടിലിൽ ഒരു സന്യാസ ജീവിതം നയിച്ചു, 1933 ആഗസ്റ്റ് ആയപ്പോഴേക്കും അദ്ദേഹം എട്ട് ഏക്കർ ഭൂമി സ്വന്തമാക്കി ആരാധനയ്ക്കായി ഒരു ചെറിയ പള്ളിയും നിർമ്മിച്ചു. ഈ കാലയളവിൽ, ഫാദർ ആൻഡ്രോണികിന്റെ ഡയറി കുറിപ്പുകളിൽ യോഹന്നാൻ കശ്ശീശായുടെ പ്രാർത്ഥനയും യാമ നമസ്കാരങ്ങളിലെ തീക്ഷ്ണതയും ശ്രദ്ധിച്ചതായി എഴുതപ്പെട്ടിട്ടുണ്ട്

The rebuilt church was consecrated on January 19, 2001 by Baselios Marthoma Mathews II Catholicos, Mathews Mar Epiphanios, Paulose Mar Milithios, and Mathews Mar Severios. This parish has contributed 3 priests to the Holy Church. Currently ,the church maintains 3 shrines and a parsonage.

81 families (2022) - The Orthodox faithful residing in and around Sooranad North, particularly near the Government High School and Kannamam Market area, were for many years members of their mother parishes—St. Thomas Orthodox Church and St. Mary's Orthodox Church, Sooranad. Due to the difficulty of travelling long distances to attend Holy Qurbana and other liturgical services, the need for a new parish gradually became evident. A plot of land, adjacent to St. Thomas U.P. School, owned by the Church, was graciously made available. After obtaining the necessary permissions, construction of the new church was initiated by dismantling an old structure within the school premises.

On 22 November 1968, under the leadership Fr. T.G. Geevarghese, the faithful formally entered the church premises. The foundation stone of the church was laid on 28 November 1968. The parish was officially established in January 1969. The consecration ceremonies were completed on 30 and 31 January 1969. Rev. Fr. T. G. Geevarghese was appointed as the first Vicar, and the parish was named St. Mary's Salem Orthodox Syrian Church, Sooranad North. Subsequently, the parish committee and various spiritual organizations were formed. From February 1969 onward, regular Holy Qurbana and worship services were conducted.

1,916 families (2022) – Consecrated in 1900 by Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni) in the presence of Malankara Metropolitan Mar Joseph Dionysius, this church became the first Syrian Christian parish established in the Thiruvananthapuram district. It later gave rise to the region's subsequent Malankara Orthodox, Mar Thoma, Malankara Catholic, and Jacobite communities, making it one of the most historically influential parishes in the capital.

On June 23, 1991, H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II elevated it to cathedral status as the episcopal seat of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese. Today, it is the largest urban parish in the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church, with more than 9,000 regularly attending parishioners.

The parish celebrates four weekly Holy Qurbanas, three additional monthly services, and maintains thirteen active prayer organizations. Its annual feast of St. George draws thousands of devotees, while the cathedral's blend of traditional Kerala and Byzantine architecture, murals, icons, and carved wooden interior reflects the artistic heritage of the Malankara Church.

Among its notable members is renowned playback singer K. J. Yesudas, who was married at this church.

ds:
Established in 2004, this mission center is home to the Mar Dioscorus College of Pharmacy, a flagship educational institution of the Charitable and Educational Society of the Thiruvananthapuram Orthodox Diocese. Named in honor of H.G. Geevarghese Mar Dioscoros, the Diocese's founding Metropolitan, it reflects the Church's commitment to higher education and professional formation.

Affiliated with the Kerala University of Health Sciences, the college offers Diploma in Pharmacy (D.Pharm), Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm), Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D), Master of Pharmacy (M.Pharm), and Ph.D. programs. It serves as one of the leading Orthodox educational institutions in Kerala, combining academic excellence with the values of Christian service and ethical healthcare.

Established in 1987, this Orthodox center serves as one of the principal spiritual gathering places of the Thiruvananthapuram Diocese.

The center hosts the annual Trivandrum Orthodox Convention, bringing together clergy and faithful each year for worship, preaching, and spiritual renewal. It remains an important venue for diocesan conventions and major ecclesiastical events.

പരിശുദ്ധ പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ തിരുശേഷിപ്പിനാൽ ധന്യമായ ആഗോള പൗരസ്ത്യ ജോർജ്ജിയൻ തീർത്ഥാടന കേന്ദ്രം:

എ.ഡി 1915 ഒക്ടോബര്‍ മാസത്തില്‍ ബഥേല്‍ സെന്റ്‌ ജോര്‍ജ്ജ്‌ പള്ളി എന്ന നാമധേയത്തില്‍ ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ പണി തുടങ്ങി 1916 ജനുവരി മാസത്തില്‍ ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ കൂദാശാ കര്‍മ്മം കാലം ചെയ്‌ത ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ കാതോലിക്കാ ബാവാ തിരുമേനി നടത്തി. പ്രസ്തുത ദേവാലയം 1919 ജൂലൈ മാസത്തില്‍ ഉണ്ടായ കാറ്റും മഴയും മൂലം ഇടിഞ്ഞുവീണു. പെട്ടെന്ന്‌ അതേ സ്ഥാനത്ത്‌ തന്നെ ദൈവാലയം പണിതു.

പുതിയ മദ്ബഹായുടെ പണി 1952 ഒക്ടോബര്‍ മാസത്തില്‍ ആരംഭിച്ചു. അതിന്റെ ഉത്തരനിരപ്പു വരെയുള്ള കെട്ട്‌ 1963-ല്‍ പൂര്‍ത്തിയായി. ഈ ഭിത്തി 12-7-1963-ല്‍ ഉണ്ടായ അതിഭയങ്കരമായ മഴ നിമിത്തം ഇടിഞ്ഞു വീഴുകയുണ്ടായി. വീണ്ടും അതേ പ്ലാനില്‍ തന്നെ ഒരു മദ്ബഹാ പണിയണമെന്നുള്ള പൊതു യോഗ തീരുമാനമനുസരിച്ച്‌ 22-8-1963-ല്‍ റവ, വൈദ്യന്‍ യോശുവ കത്തനാര്‍ അവര്‍കളാല്‍ ശിലാസ്ഥാപനം നടത്തപ്പെടുകയും തുടര്‍ന്ന്‌ പണി നടത്തപ്പെടുകയും ചെയ്തു 1971-ല്‍ പുതിയ പള്ളിയുടെ പണി ആരംഭിച്ചു. പുതിയ ദേവാലയത്തിന്‌ പോര്‍ച്ച്‌ ഉള്‍പ്പടെ 90 അടിനീളവും 27 അടി വീതിയുമുണ്ട്‌. ദേവാലയത്തിന്റെ കൂദാശ 1985 ജനുവരി 9, 10 തീയതികളില്‍ മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മാര്‍ത്തോമ്മ മാത്യൂസ്‌ പ്രഥമന്‍ കാതോലിക്കാ ബാവായുടെ പ്രധാന കാര്‍മ്മികത്വത്തിലും, മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മാര്‍ത്തോമ്മ മാത്യൂസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ കതോലിക്കാ ബാവയുടേയും (അന്ന്‌ നിയുക്ത കാതോലിക്കാ), അഭി.ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ലീസ്‌ മാര്‍ ദീയസ്‌കോറസ്‌ തിരുമേനിയുടെ സഹകരണത്തിലും നടത്തി.

ദൈവാലയത്തിന്റെ സ്ഥലപരിമിതി മനസ്സിലാക്കി ഇരുവശങ്ങള്‍ വീതി കൂട്ടുകയും, അതിനോടനുബന്ധിച്ച്‌ രണ്ട്‌ മദ്ബഹാകള്‍ നിര്‍മ്മിക്കുകയും ചെയ്തു, കുര്‍ബാന അനുഷ്ഠിക്കുവാന്‍ 5 ബലി പീഠങ്ങളുമുണ്ട്‌.

പരിശുദ്ധ ഗീവര്‍ഗ്ഗീസ്‌ സഹദായുടെ അതിശ്രേഷ്ഠമായ മദ്ധ്യസ്ഥതയുള്ള ഈ ദൈവാലയത്തെ, പൗരസ്ത്യ കാതോലിക്കായും, മലങ്കര മെത്രാ പോലീത്തയുമായ മോറോന്‍ മാര്‍ ബസ്സേലിയോസ്‌ മര്‍ത്തോമ്മ പൗലോസ്‌ ദ്വിതീയന്‍ തിരുമനസ്സുകൊണ്ട്‌ നമ്പർ 39/2011 കല്പന പ്രകാരം നല്ലില സെന്റ് ജോർജ് ഓർത്തഡോക്സ് തീർത്ഥാടന പള്ളി എന്ന പേരിൽ ജോർജ്ജിയൻ തീർത്ഥാടന കേന്ദ്രമായി ഉയർത്തപെട്ടു. 2011 മെയ്‌ 2-ാം തീയതി തീർത്ഥാടന പ്രഖ്യാപനം സമ്മേളനം നടത്തപ്പെട്ടു.

പരിശുദ്ധ എപ്പിസ്‌ക്കോപ്പന്‍ സുന്നഹദോസ്‌ ഇടവകയുടെ അപേക്ഷ പരിഗണിച്ച്‌ നമ്പര്‍ HES/HH/75/2011 കല്പന പ്രകാരം നവംബര്‍ മാസം 11-ാം തീയതി പരിശുദ്ധ പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ തിരു ശേഷിപ്പ് അഭിവന്ദ്യ സഖറിയാ മാര്‍ അന്തോണിയോസ്‌ മെത്രാപൊലീത്താ തിരുമനസ്സിന്റേയും അഭിവന്ദ്യ പൗലോസ്‌ മാര്‍ പക്കോമിയോസ്‌ തിരുമനസ്സിന്റേയും പ്രധാന കാര്‍മ്മികത്വത്തില്‍ പ്രതിഷ്ഠിക്കുകയുണ്ടായി എല്ലാ മാസവും 2-ാം ശനിയാഴ്ച ജോര്‍ജജിയന്‍ ധ്യാനവും എല്ലാ 4-ാം ശനിയാഴ്ച സന്ധ്യ നമസ്ക്കാരത്തിനു ശേഷം പരുമല തിരുമേനിയുടെ നാമത്തിൽ മദ്ധ്യസ്ഥ പ്രാര്‍ത്ഥനയും നടത്തുന്നു.

ഇപ്പോൾ ഈ ദൈവാലയത്തിൽ 435 ഭവനങ്ങൾ ഉണ്ട്. 12 കുരിശടികളും, ഒരേക്കർ 34 സെന്റ് വസ്തു വും, പള്ളിയോട് ചേർന്ന് ഒരു പാഴ്സനേജും ഉണ്ട്. പള്ളിയുടെ ചുമതലയിൽ ബഥേൽ ഇംഗ്ലീഷ് മീഡിയം സ്കൂൾ എന്ന പേരിൽ ഒരു സ്കൂളും പ്രവർത്തിച്ചു വരുന്നു. സഭയിലെ എല്ലാ ആത്മീയ സംഘടനകളും, ഇടവകയിലെ ഭവനങ്ങളെ 8 വാർഡുകളായി വിഭജിച്ച് പ്രാർഥനായോഗങ്ങളും നടന്നുവരുന്നു. ഇപ്പോൾ ഇടവകയിൽ 5 പട്ടക്കാരും മരുമക്കളായ 5 പട്ടക്കാരും ഉണ്ട്. ഫാ. ഗീവർഗ്ഗീസ്, മത്തായി, ഫാ. വി.കെ. ഡാനിയേൽ, ഫാ. , ജോഷം വൈദ്യൻ, ഫാ. പി.എം. ജോർജ്ജ്, അലക്സാണ്ടർ, ഫാ. എം. തോമസുകുട്ടി, ഫാ. സ്റ്റീഫൻ വൈരമൺ, ഫാ. ഫിലിപ്പ് മാത്യു, ഫാ. റെജി ലൂക്കോസ്, ഫാ. കെ. കെ. തോമസ്, ഫാ. വർഗ്ഗീസ് കോശി, ഫാ. ജേക്കബ് ജോർജ്, ഫാ. ജേക്കബ് പണിക്കർ, സജീവ് വർഗ്ഗീസ്, ഫാ.വി.ജി കോശി വൈദ്യൻ, ഫാ.ജോസ് എം ദാനിയേൽ, ഫാ.ജോൺ പണിക്കർ കോർ എപ്പിസ്കോപ്പ,ഫാ. മാത്യൂ എബ്രഹാം തലവൂർ എന്നിവർ വികാരിമാരായിരുന്നു. ഇപ്പോഴത്തെ വികാരിയായി ഫാ ബേസിൽ ജെ പണിക്കർ സേവനമനുഷ്ടിക്കുന്നു.

n: Thenmala Junction St. George Orthodox Shrine

ds:
Dedicated to Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni), this roadside shrine was established on land donated by Mr. P. S. Rajappan, who gifted approximately four cents of property to the parish for the erection of a granite cross.

The shrine underwent a major renovation in 1990 and was rededicated on July 8 by H.G. Thomas Mar Athanasios, Metropolitan of the Chengannur Diocese. Following the widening of the adjoining roadway in 2008, the compound wall and entrance gate were reconstructed.

498 families (2022) – Originally established as a filial parish of the Palayam Cathedral, this church is the first in Thiruvananthapuram dedicated to Saint Geevarghese Mar Gregorios (Parumala Thirumeni). Reverently known as Thekkan Parumala AKA Parumala of the South, it has become one of the principal pilgrimage churches of southern Kerala.

A chapel was established in 1976 after land was acquired in 1972, using materials from the former Sunday School building of the Palayam Cathedral. It was consecrated by H.G. Mathews Mar Coorilos, later H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II, and was raised to an independent parish in 1985.

Rapid growth led to the expansion of the original chapel in 1988 and the construction of the present church, consecrated on January 12–13, 2001, by H.H. Baselios Marthoma Mathews II. On the same occasion, the Holy Relics of Parumala Thirumeni were solemnly installed, and the church was proclaimed "Thekkan Parumala St. Gregorios Valia Pally."

The parish also established its own cemetery at Malamukal after acquiring 76 cents of land near Nettayam, replacing its earlier reliance on the Palayam Cathedral cemetery. Today, the church remains a major pilgrimage center, drawing devotees from across southern Kerala who seek the intercessions of Parumala Thirumeni regardless of caste or creed.

There are 5 priests (including one late cor-episcopa) from this parish.
